item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Steelers’ Insider offers cryptic hint after shocking Aaron Rodgers benching appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Pittsburgh Steelers stunned the NFL late Tuesday night by benching four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph their starting quarterback for Friday’s clash against the Denver Broncos. Even more surprising, the team isn’t entirely sure how its veteran signal-caller will handle the move. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, Pittsburgh left Rodgers inactive despite a clean injury report and braced for the fallout. “The #Steelers do not know how Aaron Rodgers will react to tonight’s news,” Schultz reported. “‘I guess we’ll find out together,’ a source said.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The #Steelers do not know how Aaron Rodgers will react to tonight’s news. “I guess we’ll find out together,” a source said. https://t.co/OwZdKL1OJW pic.twitter.com/s6dCsePKbo — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 25, 2026 That uncertainty makes the timing even wilder. Just one day earlier on Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy publicly backed his 42-year-old quarterback, who turns 43 next week. McCarthy won a Super Bowl alongside Rodgers with the Green Bay Packers and reunited with him in Pittsburgh for what Rodgers called his 22nd and final NFL season. However, two straight losses dropped the Steelers to 6-4 and pushed the coaching staff to hit the reset button . Across 10 starts this year, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions, posting a career-low 86.6 passer rating while taking 31 sacks. Sunday’s 19-16 road loss to the Philadelphia Eagles exposed Pittsburgh’s offensive stagnation. Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown with zero interceptions, though Philadelphia’s pass rush sacked him five times. Pittsburgh didn’t find the end zone until Rodgers hit Max Hurleman , who led the team with six catches for 61 yards, for a 20-yard score with 1:21 remaining. Rodgers also led the Steelers with 29 rushing yards, while wideout DK Metcalf managed just one catch for two yards on four targets before officials ejected him for two personal fouls. Now, Pittsburgh hands the offense to Rudolph, who owns a 9-9-1 record across 19 career starts with the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, leaving Rodgers’ future in complete limbo. item.title: 'We can win without him!' - Hansi Flick insists Barcelona can cope with Lamine Yamal injury blow ahead of Champions League clash against Sabah
item.description: FC Barcelona v Villarreal CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has challenged his squad to prove they can thrive in the absence of Lamine Yamal as the teenage sensation sits out Wednesday's Champions League trip to Sabah. The 19-year-old has been the focal point of the Blaugrana's devastating attack this term, but an ankle issue has forced him to stay behind in Spain while his teammates travel to Azerbaijan. Ankle injury ends Yamal's ever-present run Yamal has started all 17 of Barcelona's games this season, scoring 13 goals and registering 13 assists, before missing out for the first time. Monday's medical checks prompted staff to leave the 19-year-old in Spain ahead of Baku trip , though he should return for Sunday's La Liga trip to Deportivo A Coruna. Flick has yet to finalise his attack for Wednesday's tie, with Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Anthony Gordon, and Raphinha all competing to deputise. Defensive injuries further complicate selection, as Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart remain out while Pau Cubarsí is unlikely to be risked following a hip problem. Flick and De Jong back squad depth At Tuesday's pre-match press conference, Flick downplayed Yamal's absence while praising De Jong's adaptability. "We have played without Lamine in the past, we know what to do," Flick said. "He is very important for us, but [on Monday] we checked and decided it is better he stays at home. Hopefully, everything works well and he's available for the weekend." Speaking earlier, De Jong - who has made five appearances since overcoming a knee injury - backed the squad's quality. "A player like Lamine will always be missed," the midfielder said. "He is a player with extraordinary talent. He creates danger and chances on his own, so you notice when a player like him is not there. But the squad is full of good players and we can win without him." With defensive shortages potentially keeping De Jong at centre-back , Flick applauded his selflessness. "The thing I like most about Frenkie is that he said 'OK, coach, if you need me as a centre-back or a full-back, it doesn't matter,'" Flick explained. "He said he's available and he can help the team. This is, for me, a team player. He gives everything for this team. "We all know he is one of the best midfielders in the world. I see him as a midfielder, we need his quality there, but at the moment we will see where we need him tomorrow." De Jong reiterated his long-term positional preference while putting the team first: "I consider myself a midfielder, everyone knows that. I have always played there. But if team needs me elsewhere or the coach considers it better I play in another position, I will always do it." Barca chase first European crown since 2015 Barcelona enter Wednesday's clash in commanding domestic form, leading La Liga with 12 wins from 13 games. Three victories from four Champions League outings have also fuelled hopes of a first European trophy since 2015.

item.title: How to unearth young stars, the Bayern Munich way
item.description: Bayern initially aim to find young players from Bavaria before looking further afield [Getty Images] Bayern Munich are one of the elite powers in European football and current home of Ballon d'Or winner and England captain Harry Kane. But, while Kane is the latest hugely successful foreign import at Bayern, the German giants also put a particular focus on producing their own elite young talent. In 2013, Bayern had four homegrown players in the starting line-up as they won the Champions League. Repeating that victory, and continuing the club's history of nurturing young players, is what director of youth development and campus Jochen Sauer says Bayern are aiming for. Sauer joined from RB Salzburg in 2017 when the academy campus opened in another part of Munich, away from the first-team training complex. The club's motto "Mia San Mia" translates to "we are who we are" and Sauer says it has always been the club's goal to have a local homegrown element in its senior side. "It was always our identity and philosophy to be a regional club, but at the same time to be competitive internationally and on Champions League level," Sauer tells BBC Sport. "But always having a core of our team coming from the Munich area and the Bavarian region with a deep identification with the club and the city. "Our recruitment guidelines, especially for the under-11 to the under-15 teams, is trying to recruit as much talent as possible from the Munich area and the region of Bavaria." Munich-born Croatia international Josip Stanisic is a good example. The midfielder, 26, signed as an under-17 player from local outfit SC Furstenfeldbruck, while 22-year-old Aleksandar Pavlovic joined the academy aged eight and has worked his way up to the first team and is a Germany international. But perhaps the biggest name to come out of the academy in recent times is Jamal Musiala. The former Chelsea youth player, who joined aged 16, is a star for Bayern and Germany and has already won six Bundesliga titles at just 23 years old. It was part of the club's strategy to bring in the best young foreign players, and those with German passports, to the club, but they also enjoyed a bit of luck. The move came around the time Bayern Munich were interested in then-Chelsea winger Callum Hudson-Odoi, who shared the same agent as Musiala, who moved from Germany to England when he was seven. Bayern were already aware of Musiala because he was born in Germany, but the timing was right to make a deal happen. "There were for sure some pieces that came together at that time," Sauer says. "I think one reason why we fought for the player at that time was the reason we had the feeling that Chelsea is not really seeing his full potential to be a top player for their first team. "Because, otherwise, if they would have seen him as a future prospect, then it would been hard, even for Bayern Munich, to get a player out of the Chelsea environment." item.title: Key Barcelona defender unlikely to start against Sabah despite being fit – report
item.description: Key Barcelona defender unlikely to start against Sabah despite being fit – report Pau Cubarsi is expected to start on the bench when Barcelona face Sabah in the Champions League later today, as Hansi Flick looks to protect the young centre-back following his recent muscular problem. According to Mundo Deportivo , the defender is available for selection, but the Barcelona manager would prefer to give him additional time to recover fully. The 19-year-old has already missed Barcelona’s recent fixture against Villarreal after suffering an iliopsoas overload during the recent international break. With the Catalans facing a demanding schedule , Flick is unlikely to take unnecessary risks with one of his most important defensive players. Flick prioritises Cubarsi’s recovery after injury Cubarsi sustained the problem during Spain’s match against England in the previous international break. Cubarsi could start on the bench against Sabah. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) He was forced to finish the game early , and subsequent tests confirmed an overload in his iliopsoas muscle, located in the hip region. The centre-back was subsequently left out of Barcelona’s starting lineup against Villarreal, with Flick opting for a makeshift defensive partnership instead. Speaking ahead of the Sabah match , Flick confirmed that Cubarsi could play but indicated that resting him would be the preferred option if the team could manage without him. “He can play, he’s available. It’s nothing serious, nothing major or dangerous, but perhaps he could rest a little longer. If we can manage without him, we will. If we need him, he’s available,” the German admitted. Barcelona consider defensive changes against Sabah In Cubarsi’s absence against Villarreal, Flick deployed Frenkie de Jong alongside Gerard Martin in central defence, while Eric Garcia operated at right-back. Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) That arrangement could change in Baku if Jules Kounde is available to return to the starting lineup. The French defender’s potential involvement would give Flick another option at right-back and allow him to reconsider Eric Garcia’s position. One possible arrangement would see Kounde occupy the right side of defence, with Eric Garcia partnering Gerard Martin in the centre. However, the final selection has not been confirmed, and Flick could still decide to retain De Jong in defence.

item.title: Eduard Löwen powers San Jose to first playoff win in 14 years
item.description: Eduard Löwen powers San Jose to first playoff win in 14 years By Harrison Hamm San Jose Earthquakes fans have been awaiting this moment for a generation. In the first-ever Audi MLS Cup Playoffs game at PayPal Park on Tuesday night, summer signing Eduard Löwen delivered a stunning long-range free kick that proved the difference in the Quakes' 2-1 win over Houston Dynamo FC , just a day after being named the 2026 MLS Comeback Player of the Year . The Game 1 victory in their Western Conference Round One Best-of-3 Series marked San Jose's first Audi MLS Cup Playoffs since 2012 and puts the Earthquakes one win away from advancing in the postseason for the first time since 2010. “We had a really good performance,” Löwen told Apple TV postgame. “We played well. We were the better team." Lovely Löwen With San Jose leading 1-0 courtesy of captain Ronaldo Vieira 's first MLS goal, Löwen unleashed one of the most impressive strikes of the playoffs so far. His free kick from distance caromed in off the post past Jonathan Bond , mere minutes after Bond had made a diving stop to deny another Löwen free kick. “It's definitely high up,” Löwen said of where the goal ranks in his career tallies. “It's definitely high up in the category. I'm thankful that the second one went in. Credit to the goalkeeper on the first one. That was an amazing save, and I thought I'd go the same way again. But then I thought maybe I'd try the other way." Since being acquired in August from St. Louis CITY SC , Löwen has established himself as an integral piece of the Quakes’ midfield, as he proved at both ends of the pitch on Tuesday night with a goal-line clearance to preserve San Jose's lead shortly before going on to double the advantage with his first playoff goal. Löwen's success in San Jose follows a time of significant personal adversity during which he stepped away from professional soccer last year to care for his wife, Ilona, who passed away in March after two years of brain cancer treatment. The German playmaker returned to the sport this season and has excelled, earning recognition as the Comeback Player of the Year. Now, he is helping lead the way as the Quakes look to go somewhere they haven’t been in more than a decade. “Everything’s new here,” legendary head coach Bruce Arena said after the game. “We’re learning to be a good club. We’re learning to be a good team. Anything where we’re moving in a good direction is positive.” Headed to Houston San Jose can close out the Round One Best-of-3 Series in Game 2 on Saturday at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston, where a win would send them to the Western Conference Semifinals (2:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). If Houston claim victory, it would force a decisive Game 3 back at PayPal Park on Dec. 2. “We're gonna take the win and go to Houston and try to end the series in Houston,” Arena said. “It's gonna be a hell of a battle.” WATCH: Eduard Löwen guides San Jose Earthquakes to Game 1 win over Houston

item.title: Why The NFL Is Bringing U2 And Wu-Tang Clan To Thanksgiving Football
item.description: The NFL logo is seen on the field. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images The NFL on Thanksgiving isn’t going to challenge the Super Bowl anytime soon But Thanksgiving offers something the Super Bowl does not: multiple games, more entertainment and a direct connection to holiday shopping. This year, for the first time, the NFL will air games on Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday. And the games will create a large-scale entertainment platform for Wu-Tang Clan, U2, Miranda Lambert, and the Goo Goo Dolls, all of whom are performing in some capacity amid the five (count ‘em, five) games blitzing streaming and linear broadcast networks. The festivities begin when the Packers and Rams clash in the inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix. Here’s why the NFL on Thanksgiving is now the place to see the band that changed rap forever with Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers) : the NFL has already won the battle for sports fans. Thanksgiving week is about the NFL embedding itself into popular culture through entertainment and commerce, which attracts viewers beyond sports enthusiasts. From Doubleheaders to Dolly Parton The NFL has come a long way since Thanksgiving meant watching the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys square off against different opponents on network TV with nothing particularly noteworthy happening at halftime. Dolly Parton creating a cultural moment (and arguably eclipsing the game itself) by appearing in a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader uniform as she did in 2023 was unthinkable. But the tradition began to change over a period of years, beginning when the NFL added a third Thanksgiving game in 2006. The rise of streaming was the catalyst that pushed the NFL to another level of entertainment and football. The launch of Amazon’s Black Friday game in 2023 marked the first time the NFL expanded its holiday programming beyond Thanksgiving Day. And that year, the NFL began a sustained pattern of promoting three major musical headliners across all three Thanksgiving Day games. The streaming businesses have had good reason to muscle their way into the Thanksgiving tradition. The NFL is by far the most popular programming on American television, averaging roughly 18.7 million viewers per game during the 2025 regular season and continuing to draw huge audiences into the 2026 season. Streaming businesses, facing viewer saturation, need to monetize audiences more effectively with advertising, and advertising means competing with traditional television networks for the kinds of programming that attract large, predictable audiences. NFL football delivers those audiences at a time when retailers and consumer brands are spending heavily to capture holiday shoppers. Netflix also gives the NFL the means to export a distinctly American tradition to the rest of the world. He also explained why he chose to carry the public backlash alone for now. Bancroft's changed mood has given him some comfort after painful days. Sandpapergate row: Usman Khawaja reveals how he offered to be the 'bad guy' so Cameron Bancroft could speak out Cameron Bancroft has told Usman Khawaja that he will be "forever grateful" for the part the batter played in allowing him to speak about Sandpapergate. The details came out in a long interview on The Grade Cricketer podcast, which was Khawaja's first major long-form conversation since Pat Cummins held a marathon press conference in Sydney, and since Bancroft published his own confession. Khawaja's memoir, Sabr, had reopened the 2018 ball-tampering scandal a few weeks earlier, and his claim that the whole team knew about it has divided the Australian dressing room ever since. Cummins spoke for 68 minutes on November 13, 2026, and described the allegations as "100% wrong" and "complete and utter nonsense". The reaction left Khawaja shut inside his hotel room for an entire day, unable to face anyone, until a text from Bancroft arrived a day or two later and lifted his mood. Khawaja described why he kept names out of the book and his account gives a rare look at the private side of a dispute that has played out loudly in public. As the first person to talk about the subject, Khawaja expected to take the hardest hits, and the first message from Bancroft came on the day that the claims broke. "I went in there with eyes wide open. I knew the first guy that was going to talk about this, and that was me, was always going to get nailed," he said. "But that day I had a message from Cameron Bancroft, and it was a thank-you message. One thing I'll never forget from that message is he said to me, 'Uzzie, you've done the right thing, and I appreciate it more than you can ever imagine.' I really needed that at that point because I was nowhere that first day." The two men spoke on the phone the following day, and Khawaja checked in on how his friend was coping. "I remember I talked to him on the phone," he said. "I asked, 'Are you all right, mate? How are you going?' item.title: Players in limbo after NZ netball league collapses
item.description: Mason has played professionally for six years [Getty Images] All Parris Mason has known is playing netball. But with a World Cup just nine months away, she and four other New Zealand players have been left in limbo after the collapse of their domestic league. "There's a high potential I will not be playing netball heading into a World Cup," she told BBC Sport. While a significant number of her Silver Ferns team-mates play professionally in Australia and England, Mason stayed with her home league. The 23-year-old defender, who has been a full-time professional for six years, found out her netball fate when the news was leaked to the media. "It shattered me," she said. "The influx of emotions; is my career over? What do I do next? It was just so much to handle all at once." Netball New Zealand admitted the way events unfolded publicly was deeply regrettable and has pledged to support the affected players. "We know this period of uncertainty has been extremely tough for players, coaches, teams and everyone involved in the domestic competition," a statement said. "Their wellbeing is our priority, and we are working closely with the New Zealand Netball Players' Association to support them." It comes as the Silver Ferns are on the cusp of becoming the world's number one ranked side, after winning gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and beating Australia in the Constellation Cup. The World Cup will be held in Sydney, Australia, between 25 August and 5 September, with New Zealand looking to win the title for a sixth time. What happened to the ANZ Premiership? There had been uncertainty over the future of the ANZ Premiership for a couple years. The league had struggled to secure long-term broadcast deals which impacted the league financially. In 2026, the league recorded a loss of around $NZ 3.7m (£1.5m). There was an exodus of the country's best players. Ten of the 12 Silver Ferns who won gold for New Zealand at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow have moved overseas to play - primarily in Australia. Businesswoman Anna Mowbray and her husband, former All Blacks player Ali Williams, pitched a new private league for 2027, but negotiations fell through just eight weeks after signing a term sheet. "I don't understand my life without netball," said Mason. "It's been a big part of my identity, and [there is a] mental toll to [being] continually knocked down. "I think of everything in this whole situation as just completely sad." Nathan Limm, who has been following the story for the New Zealand Herald said: "The Ferns' success feels a little bit fragile. item.title: Nick Wright’s Patrick Mahomes take gets trolled in his latest NFL quarterback ranking
item.description: Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images Nick Wright’s latest NFL quarterback rankings sparked a debate, where his Patrick Mahomes take got brutally trolled. Patrick Mahomes has done a brilliant job in recent weeks to keep a patched-up Kansas City Chiefs afloat by turning back the clock. He is clearly not ready to relinquish his throne as the quarterback to usurp in this league, but several contenders are gunning for it. Nick Wright felt that contendership and more after his latest Patrick Mahomes take got trolled by the whole studio. Nick Wright puts Patrick Mahomes top of the mountain Wright creates a “Mahomes Mountain” at the end of every gameweek in the NFL, and as the name suggests, it ranks the quarterbacks in the league. Being named Mahomes Mountain has nothing to do with the ranking of Mahomes, but Wright perhaps took the name a bit too literally in his latest ranking. Speaking on First Things First , Wright ranked the quarterbacks, and put Mahomes at the top, ahead of Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in the tier just below. While Mahomes has undoubtedly been elite again this season, this take didn’t go down well with the rest of his studio, who vouched for Purdy to be at the top. It got so comedic that Wright’s own takes were replayed back to him, which he gave when the 49ers completed a dominant win against the Vikings, courtesy of a perfect Purdy performance. He said at the time that Purdy is the league MVP, which naturally means that he is the best quarterback in the league as well! Here’s what Wright said to justify placing Mahomes at the top: “He was a man who for the 2nd time in his career, just had a 4-game stretch, averaging 300 yards per game, averaging more than 3 touchdowns per game with no turnovers, which has only been done in his career by one other person, Aaron Rodgers.” Wright’s previous comments were immediately played back to him, and he played it off as choosing between two elites, saying two things swayed him – Broussard saying Purdy wasn’t the MVP, and him saying Purdy was the best quarterback in the NFC. How that makes sense is left up to the reader, because Wright didn’t seem very convinced about it either! item.title: ‘Got to be…’ – Maxx Crosby sounds off on Bijan Robinson’s take about the easiest position in the NFL
item.description: Credit: Emilee Chinn/Aric Becker / AFP via Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders DE Maxx Crosby did not appreciate Atlanta Falcons RB Bijan Robinson’s take that the edge rusher is the easiest position in the NFL. Every elite or contending team is looking to build their offence around a world-class QB and their defence around a world-class edge rusher. Defensive players usually play within a system, so the EDGE is the one defender who is designed to be an independent unit responsible for sacking a slow QB. Unfortunately, the limited scope of the role led to Falcons RB Robinson dismissing the position as the easiest in the NFL, irking standout EDGE Crosby. Maxx Crosby slams Bijan Robinson’s ‘casual a– take’ Crosby, a former All-Pro EDGE, responded to Robinson’s thoughts on ‘The Rush Podcast,’ justifying their value while tearing down the position Robinson stars in. “Casual a– take. Look at it like this: who is your highest-paid player (QB)? And who is next (EDGE)? If it were easy to play the position and get one sack a game, why doesn’t everybody do it? Out of 1,000 snaps, getting 10 sacks is great. You’re considered elite. Running back? You get handed the ball, and you go play football. You run, and you catch. Running back is, easily, got to be the easiest position to play.” It might be easier to be an average EDGE than an average RB, but the top-tier EDGEs are more valuable because of how scarce the talent at the highest level is, compared to productive RBs being more available. EDGEs also create plays actively detrimental to another team while having longer careers on average than RBs, so Crosby’s point cannot be ignored. What did Bijan Robinson say? Robinson spoke on the St. Brown Podcast, hosted by Lions RB Amon-Ra St. Brown, and shared his harsh take on edge rushers in the NFL. “I would say D-Line. Edge rusher. You have one job, get past the tackle. You don’t have too much responsibility, especially if you’re one who has to rush the passer, I would say that’s the easiest. One sack a game.” Crosby is on a three-year, $106.5 million contract, earning $35.8 million with the Raiders in the 2026-27 season. item.title: Pep Guardiola admits he was 'embarrassed' to reject Italy job as former Man City boss confirms national team management is his 'next step'
item.description: Bournemouth v Manchester City - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Pep Guardiola has broken his silence on his decision to turn down the opportunity to manage Italy, admitting he felt "embarrassed" to say no to the Azzurri. The legendary tactician, currently on a sabbatical following a trophy-laden decade at Manchester City, also confirmed that his next move in football will be onto the international stage. Italy approached Guardiola after third straight World Cup miss In July, after Italy missed a third consecutive World Cup, the Italian federation (FIGC) sent Paolo Maldini and Leonardo to approach Guardiola . The offer arrived shortly after he left Manchester City following a 2016–2026 stint yielding six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and a Champions League crown. Drained by the grind, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager chose a self-imposed sabbatical of at least one year. Italy subsequently re-hired Roberto Mancini , their Euro 2020-winning coach from 2018 to 2023. Guardiola opens up on emotional Azzurri refusal Speaking on Romario TV on Tuesday with Brazil legend and former Barcelona team-mate Romario, Guardiola explained why timing scuppered the Italy move. He also confirmed his desire to eventually coach internationally while insisting he remains content away from the touchline. "This is the first time I speak about this, but yes, I did talk to them," Guardiola said. "I felt embarrassed to say 'no' to Italy, a country like Italy, it would have been one of the greatest honours of my career to coach the Italian national team. But I realised I needed to stop. If they had called two years earlier, I probably would have accepted. "But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop. I needed some time for myself. After 18 years as a coach, with matches every three days, week in and week out, there comes a moment when you just have to say 'phew.'" Identifying "a national team" as his sole unfulfilled coaching ambition - and "that is the next step" for his career - Guardiola stressed he is in no rush to return. "The truth is, I don't know, I really don't know. But for now, I'm doing fine," he added. "If I ever return, it will be because my gut tells me to, and because someone wants me, then I'll go back. But it's been many years, so many matches." At his final press conference, Pochettino called it "the perfect moment to arrive" at the USMNT and urged Guardiola to take the job: "Everything is in the right direction. item.title: New manager, fresh hope. But why the stats say Al Faisaly don't need overhaul
item.description: New manager, fresh hope. But why the stats say Al Faisaly don't need overhaul feature Mohamed Dahman replaces Giovanni Solinas in the dugout ahead of his debut match against fellow new boys Diriyah Club It might seem a rather obvious statement, but football is all about goals. The important distinction, however, is it is just as important to deny them as it is to score them. Just look at promoted sides Al Faisaly and Diriyah Club . Both started the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League with different expectations and ambitions. Yet despite Diriyah Club signing Darwin Nunez , it is actually Al Faisaly that has scored the more goals this season out of the two - 13 goals to 10. The issue is, though, that Al Faisaly have conceded almost twice as many (24 to 13) and that is the story of their respective campaigns so far. Mohamed Dahman takes temporary charge of Al Faisaly following Giovanni Solinas' resignation There is much to like in how the Al Majma’ah-based side have played and, although manager Giovanni Solinas recently resigned, his interim replacement, Mohamed Dahman, inherits a squad that is already halfway there. At present, Al Faisaly are the league’s No.1-ranked pressing team, applying high-pressure to 46.3 percent of opposition touches, yet their opponents complete 79.2% of passes under that pressure. The former is proof they have the style right; they now just need to increase its effectiveness. That is, forcing more errors and turning the ball over more often. That’s easier said than done, of course, but it’s a better place to start than the alternative. Giovanni Solinas leaves Al Faisaly with the club one spot above the relegation zone The key focus for Dahman against Diriyah Club when the two RSL new boys meet in Matchweek 13 on Thursday must be on how the hosts start the game. That’s because the statistics reveal that Al Faisaly have conceded a league-high number of goals (14) in the first half. Drilling down even further, 13 of those have been conceded in the opening 30 minutes - also a league high - and eight between minutes 16 and 30. That latter? You guessed it, a league high. Contrast that to Diriyah Club, who are yet to give away a goal in the opening 15 minutes, and have conceded only six in the first half, and the contrast hits home. “We exploited the opposition’s defensive confusion after the first goal,” explained Al Fayha coach Fabio Carille late last month, after his team’s Sudair Derby success against Al Faisaly . So, for Al Faisaly, tightening their belts defensively must be priority No.1. That said, it’s not through lack of effort: they sit second for tackles and third for interceptions in the RSL this season. They’re pressing high, they’re winning tackles and intercepting the ball but, despite all of that, they still have the league’s third-worst defensive record. Yet it’s not all bad news. item.description: Nov 24, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; The Vegas Golden Knights celebrate a goal by forward Trevor Connelly (24) during the first period against the Edmonton Oilers at Rogers Place. EDMONTON—It is almost shocking that Trevor Connelly is not discussed more often when discussing favorites for the Calder Trophy. While there are certainly deserving candidates, Connelly has consistently stayed at or near the top among all rookies in goals and points. Even on a contending team like the Vegas Golden Knights have been year in and year out, Connelly has gone from the prospect Kelly McCrimmon refused to move to one of the most electrifying weapons the team has in their arsenal. Head coach Ryan Craig has already placed an immense amount of trust in Connelly since their days together in Henderson, and the rookie has done nothing but earn every bit of the praise he has received. With the Golden Knights in the only game of the night on Tuesday, Connelly introduced himself on the national stage with a convincing effort in his first foray against the Edmonton Oilers, as the Golden Knights battled to a 5-3 victory at Rogers Place. Early on, the Oilers looked the part of a team returning home from a six-game road trip. A high sticking penalty from Oilers defenseman Mattias Ekholm would give the Golden Knights a double minor to work with, and the power play would ultimately take advantage. Jack Eichel would land a perfectly placed shot from the left faceoff dot to the far post, beating goaltender Devon Levi to break the ice. item.description: “Only one club in Manchester”: former Man United star Rasmus Hojlund taunts rivals after Champions League strike Manchester United have had the most difficult start to a season in memory. item.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images The Joe Burrow MVP campaign recently hit a roadblock with a loss to the Washington Commanders, and Stephen A. Smith noticed an ‘aberration’. Coming into the game against the Washington Commanders, Joe Burrow’s Cincinnati Bengals were the clear favourites. Not only did the Bengals lose, but Burrow’s counterpart, Jayden Daniels, outperformed him to put a huge dent in his MVP campaign. Stephen A. Smith noticed something “not normal” with Burrow that he’s convinced won’t happen again. Stephen A. Smith on Joe Burrow’s ‘aberration’ Burrow was putting up some truly historic stats coming into the Commanders game this season, so the law of averages was bound to come up at some point. Unfortunately for him, it came up in a game his team were clear favourites for, and he couldn’t do anything to prevent it. Common sense dictates that the historic stats he was putting up before this game weren’t sustainable, but neither is the poor game against the Commanders. Stephen A. Smith is convinced of the latter, which is why he picked out some stats of Burrow from the game and said it’s “not normal” what happened to him. Speaking on ESPN , he said: “The flip side to this is that you lose 22 to 20. And how many people are going to be able to hold Joe Burrow in that offence to 20 points? It’s an aberration. It’s not normal.” Smith added that Burrow will bounce back, and his team will prepare him better to counter defences like the one he faced against the Commanders. Ultimately, Burrow has proven beyond doubt that he’s an elite quarterback, so this game was a blip more than a judgement on his abilities. The Bengals still remain the favourites for the playoffs, and Burrow will play a huge role in what happens with them once they get there. item.title: Earthquakes make successful return to MLS playoffs with victory over Houston
item.description: Earthquakes midfielder Eduard Löwen celebrates with midfielder Niko Tsakiris after scoring a goal against Dynamo during the first half of Tuesday's MLS playoff match in San Jose. (Justine Willard/Associated Press) Before Tuesday, it had been 14 long years since the San Jose Earthquakes had given their fans the experience of thunderous, high-pressure atmosphere of playoff soccer at home - and 23 even longer years since Quakes fans bore witness to a home playoff victory, when Landon Donovan rocketed a Golden Goal past Kansas City Wizards goalie Pat Onstead in sudden-death overtime to send San Jose to the MLS Cup they would eventually capture. So it was only right that in their first playoff match since 2020 and their first ever in PayPal Park, the Earthquakes gave the dedicated fans who ignored oncoming storms and persevered through mind-numbing I-280 traffic a 2-1 victory over the Houston Dynamos to take the first leg of the best-of-three Round 1 series. And the Quakes didn't keep their fans in suspense, getting the long-awaited party started early. After left midfielder Beau Leroux won a corner kick patrolling the Dynamos box, ace striker Timo Werner delivered the ball to the near post, where central midfielder and captain Ronaldo Vierra headed it in, prompting the San Jose Ultras section to whip off their shirts and as San Jose took a 1-0 lead 11 minutes into the match. Just 13 minutes later, as the drummers in the Epicentro fan section banged louder and louder, MLS Comeback Player of the Year Eduard Löwen squared up for a free kick a few yards outside the Dynamos box and rifled the ball over the Houston defenders, ricocheting the rock off the left post to extend the San Jose lead to 2-0. And though the stadium grew tense after the Dynamos' Duncan McGuire found the back of the net at the 80-minute mark, San Jose held on through regulation and five minutes of stoppage time to collect its first home playoff victory in PayPal Park's history, earning a standing ovation from the Quakes fans. item.description: Former England captain Ben Stokes and Australian batter Cameron Bancroft are among the overseas players who have registered for the IPL auction, news agency PTI reported. The auction is scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16. Stokes, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, has set his base price at Rs 2 crore. The all-rounder last played in the IPL in 2023, turning out for Chennai Super Kings in two matches. He has also represented Rajasthan Royals and the now-defunct Rising Pune Supergiant. Bancroft, who has been in the news following fresh revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, has registered at a base price of Rs 75 lakh. The 34-year-old recently sought to clarify his role in the controversy and responded to claims made by Australia captain Pat Cummins. He has never played in the IPL but regularly features in the Big Bash League (BBL). Another Australian, fast bowler Scott Boland, has also entered the auction. However, he is not expected to be available for most of the tournament. No Mustafizur, but 11 Bangladesh players register for IPL auction As many as 11 Bangladesh players have registered for the auction, but fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman is not among them. Rahman was released by Kolkata Knight Riders on the BCCI's instructions last year. The development eventually led to Bangladesh withdrawing from the T20 World Cup in India. The Bangladesh players in the auction register are Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Towhid Hridoy and Md Rubel. The 10 franchises have a maximum of 66 slots to fill, of which 25 are reserved for overseas players. The list is expected to be cut down significantly before the auction. item.title: Notre Dame’s place in the CFP rankings is still very fluid
item.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 21: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish take the field prior to the game against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs at Notre Dame Stadium on November 21, 2026 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Notre Dame fans learned all too well last year that the college football playoff rankings are something more of an art form than science. It’s funny how a body that proclaims it uses a handful of metrics eventually falls apart due to odd formatting and embedded notions about who is actually good — and made up reasons to support made up reasons. The art is terrible, and the math never has the work actually shown. Notre Dame is currently No. 4 with one game left for them, but two weeks of college football still left to be played. More than any other team in the rankings, Notre Dame is vulnerable because they are who they are. The Irish have a seat, a strong voice, ands a vote at the CFP table — but they are certainly outnumbered in sentiment. But that’s the preamble for disaster which is damn near impossible right now. Still… Notre Dame could still find themselves ranked lower than No. 4 when the final rankings are released, but they could also find themselves as the No. 2 team. It’s weird man, but there are still all of these games to be played, and we don’t know how this will all end up. It frustrates me to no end that so many look at these brackets they publish based off of the latest set of rankings and call them a “projection.” It’s not a projection — it’s a reflection of the current seeding of which NO ONE expects to be the same in a few weeks. There’s also the argument/debate between Notre Dame fans about what’s better, a bye or a first round game? There were several questions in the comments of the announcement post, that I want to answer. I think if it’s Wake Forest that wins the ACC championship with a 12-1 record, they will jump into the top 4. Texas will drop one spot if they lose the SEC Championship. Of course… Duke could beat Wake Forest and Texas A&M could beat Texas this week, and none of that matters. The rankings are still very, very fluid and all Notre Dame can do is win on Saturday and see how this lines up. A win guarantees a place in the CFP, and that is all they were expecting last year before they were screwed out of the opportunity. Let’s just see how this goes.

item.title: Nick Young calls Gilbert Arenas and Baron Davis ‘washed’ for never winning an NBA championship
item.description: Credit: Amanda Edwards/Roy Rochlin for Fanatics via Getty Images In the continuing conversation about what defines true success in the NBA, Nick Young has now made an emphatic point about players without championships. With a lot of former players now in the media space, one of the conversations which has come up is how much championship rings matter. There has been an ongoing debate about whether a role player with a ring is more of a winner than an All-Star who was never able to get one. On Gil’s Arena, Nick Young is a perfect example of the former. Despite never having been a star, he did win a championship with the 2017-18 Golden State Warriors. Gilbert Arenas and Baron Davis represent the latter. This dynamic recently led to a heated exchange, with Young going off on the two former All-Stars. Nick Young says ‘three good years’ doesn’t mean Gilbert Arenas and Baron Davis are better than him Players’ legacies in the modern NBA have become complicated. Individual accolades versus team success is a real conversation, and the basketball world cannot seem to agree on what matters more. Young seems to be clear on what he feels, though, going off on a huge rant about it. “All the accolades in the world. If you never win, you can’t be s***,” Young said. “You can never be compared to Jordan and Kobe. You can be top 10, but you’ll never be one. If another n**** wins, you get dropped down. “You can’t say you’re better than me. You n***** went to other teams, and y’all were f****** trash. Y’all, 3 good years, then became WASHED. Y’all can’t beat me. You n***** only had 3 good years and then became WASHED. Stop downplaying my s***. Y’all Vanilla Ice. You can never be Eminem. You’ll never be in rooms with champions like me.” This was quite the expressive take from Young, and one that Arenas and Davis naturally disagreed with. Ultimately, championships count heavily for stars who were crucial to getting them. Basketball is a team sport and everyone’s contribution counts, but to say that a role player with a ring had a better career than a multiple-time All-Star without one is going a bit too far. item.title: Geno Auriemma at a loss after UConn’s loss to rival South Carolina: ‘I have to figure it out’
item.description: UNCASVILLE, Conn. — After spending the majority of his career making opposing coaches uncomfortable, legendary UConn coach Geno Auriemma met his match. Dawn Staley’s Gamecocks, the No. 1 team in the country, delivered a tough lesson to No. 7 UConn on Tuesday. Auriemma was as despondent as he’s been all season following UConn’s 65-56 loss that dropped the Huskies to 4-3 on the season. “You might be able to tell that and I’m having a really hard time coaching this team, and I have to figure it out,” Auriemma said. “But it’d be nice if I got a little help.” Auriemma seemed embarrassed after losing to No. 5 Michigan by 11 on Nov. 5. He was annoyed when UConn fell to No. 7 Louisville, 69-51, a week and a half later. Geno Auriemma talks to center Olivia Vukosa (second from left) during UConn’s 65-56 loss to South Carolina on Nov. 24, 2026, in Uncasville, Conn. AP But Auriemma had no explanation for what transpired against the Gamecocks, a team that should bring out the best in his group. “It’s already hard enough to beat the best team in the country when you are actually beating yourself,” Auriemma said. “It’s incredibly frustrating and just at a loss. Usually I have a pretty good idea but …” Auriemma doesn’t at this time. He questioned his team’s mental toughness. The final score may suggest a competitive game. But the second quarter told the real story of the night. The Huskies, playing without KK Arnold and Kayleigh Heckel, won the first quarter, 16-11. But the Gamecocks took over and never looked back while winning for the seventh time in the past 10 meetings of this rivalry. South Carolina upped its defensive intensity and started hitting shots. UConn fouled too much, missed layups and allowed Tessa Johnson and Agot Makeer to get hot from deep in that second quarter. The Gamecocks, despite being without Joyce Edwards (sickness), outscored UConn 27-6 in the second quarter and went on a 15-0 run to close the first half and lead by 16 at halftime. That was the game. Johnson scored 32 points, surpassing her career high she set earlier this month in the Gamecocks’ win against No. 3 USC. Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley shake hands before South Carolina’s road victory over UConn. AP “It feels great to get a win,” Staley said. “And it feels super great for a player like Tessa who works extremely hard. What you’re seeing is a product of a player that is always in the gym.” Players would like you to believe that South Carolina-UConn is just another game. But Tuesday added another layer in one of college basketball’s greatest rivalries. “It feels good,” said Ashlyn Watkins, who stepped up in a big way in Edwards’ absence. “It’s still early in the season, so we’re going to see them again, probably, but we’re ready for sure.” Tuesday was the first meeting since Auriemma and Staley’s fiery sideline spat in the final seconds of South Carolina’s national semifinal win in April. The two hadn’t spoken since the incident , Auriemma told reporters Sunday. Tessa Johnson

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
